subject: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation
content:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@acme-cloud.com, ops-admin@edge-partner.io
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation

Team / Acme,

We have a final opportunity to run a focused "wet-run" for the VPC/on-prem handoff tomorrow (09/06) between 1400-1600 UTC. This is not the full cutover window — it is a controlled end-to-end rehearsal that exercises the exact steps we will run during go-live:

- BGP session bring-up with Acme transit (announce/withdraw test prefixes)
- Firewall whitelist verification and ACL ramp (ingress/egress)
- KV cache priming sequence against a mirror of customer traffic (low-volume)
- Observability sampling and alert validation (latency, 95/99, token throughput)
- Controlled failover to fallback model variant if env mismatch detected

Attached: runbook_transition_wetrun_v1.pdf (primary play), preflight_acl_matrix.csv (whitelist IPs we expect). Please review the run checklist and confirm:

1) Who will own BGP commands on your side? (Acme)
2) Which firewall pair will accept our ingress CIDRs? (we've prefilled likely ranges in the CSV)
3) Ops on-call names and phone numbers for the 1400-1600 window.

Acceptance criteria to mark the wet-run successful (we will use these to gate go/no-go):
- All expected BGP prefixes seen by 1405 UTC, no unexpected route flaps for 10 minutes
- KV cache priming completes with <1% error rate for mirrored requests
- No 5xx spikes in the streaming path; avg token latency within ±15% of baseline

If we hit the acceptance criteria we will schedule the full cutover dry-run on 09/08. If not, we record blockers and run a focused remediation in the following 48h.

Sofia Ivanova
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@acme-cloud.com, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation

Thanks Sofia — quick questions inline: 

- BGP: which ASN pairs are we testing? The runbook references peering-ops-asn (65050) but Acme's transit note showed 64500 in their earlier doc. We need a confirmed mapping to avoid colliding announcements.
- ACL matrix: do we need to open any additional ephemeral ports for KV priming (TCP 11000-11010)? If so, let's add them to the CSV and request temporary firewall window.
- KV priming: what is the exact RPS we want to mirror? The runtime team suggested 50 rps sustained for 5 minutes to be meaningful without straining the mirror.

If Acme confirms ASN and firewall acceptance, I can run the BGP scripts from our side and coordinate the priming job with Connor.

-Aditya
Lead Network Engineer
aditya@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation

Hi Sofia / Aditya,

We can confirm the following for the wet-run:
- Acme transit ASN: 64500. We will accept BGP from Redwood ASN 65050 for the test session. Our peering engineer (Lina Başar) will be on the bridge and will own the BGP commands.
- Firewall pair 'EU-WEST-2-FW-A/B' will accept the Redwood ingress CIDRs listed in your CSV. We'll create a temporary rule set named RW-WETRUN-0906 with the requested ports; please confirm exact ephemeral port range if needed.
- We will have two engineers available on the bridge: lina@acme-cloud.com (BGP), victor@acme-cloud.com (firewall).

For KV priming: 50 rps sustained for 5 minutes is fine. We will also mirror request headers so you can validate cache hit ratios.

Linking to our firewall ticket: https://acme-cloud.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-4123

— Acme Network Ops
"Lina Başar" on behalf of Acme Cloud Engineering
eng@acme-cloud.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@acme-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation

Thanks — notes from runtime/obs side: 

- Telemetry: I'll be running a focused dashboard sampling during the window. Key metrics: token_latency_p50/p95/p99, streaming_error_rate, kv_priming_hit_ratio. I'll post sampling links to the bridge at +10m and +30m into the run.
- Canary traffic: we'll route mirrored traffic to the mirror pool (mirror-priming-eu) at 5x the test RPS to validate behavior under a slight surge. If we see error rate >1.5% we will throttle down and declare a block.
- Post-run: please capture tcpdump snippets of BGP session bring-up (first 2 minutes) and export the KV priming log (smoke-results-20270905.txt) — attach to the Jira ticket.

I concur with the acceptance criteria. If BGP is stable and KV priming passes we should be able to proceed to the full dry-run.

Marcus Lin
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@acme-cloud.com, ops-admin@edge-partner.io
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 16:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transition coda: wet-run for network handoff and smoke validation — final plan and go-ahead

All — quick readout from the bridge:

- BGP: Lina (Acme) and Aditya completed the session bring-up at 14:03 UTC. All test prefixes seen by 14:05 UTC. No route flaps observed in the 15m monitoring window.
- ACLs: EU-WEST-2-FW-A/B applied RW-WETRUN-0906 as requested; ephemeral ports 11000-11010 were opened for the priming job then removed after completion.
- KV priming: Ran 50 rps for 5 minutes against mirror-priming-eu, hit ratio 98.7% (error rate 0.8%).
- Telemetry: p95 token latency +11% vs baseline (within acceptance). streaming_error_rate stayed below 0.5%.
- Artifacts: smoke-results-20270905.txt (attached), tcpdump snippet (on the Jira ticket).

Conclusion: wet-run PASSED acceptance criteria. I'm authorizing scheduling of the full dry-run on 2027-09-08. If anyone has objections to that date please raise them in the next 12 hours.

Thanks everyone for a crisp execution.

Sofia
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_transition_wetrun_v1.pdf (pdf), preflight_acl_matrix.csv (csv), smoke-results-20270905.txt (log)
